To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Wnt1, Wnt3a promote hES cell proliferation and self-renewal in the presence of feeder cell-derived self-renewing factors and that over-expression of Wnt3a enhances the ability of HFAfi cells to support hES cell growth and self-renew.
Wnt3A, Wnt1 and bFGF can promote the proliferation of human embryonic stem cells, and that immortalized engineered feeder cell lines can be used to efficiently make genetic-modified hES cell lines.

1) Wnt3a stimulates hES cell proliferation and affects cell fate determination; 2) Wnt3 and Wnt1 enhance the proliferation of undiffereniated hES cells under feeder cell derived factors and bFGFs; 3) Wnt3 over-expression enhances the ability of immortalized feeder cells to support undifferentiated hESC growth and enables us to select rare drug-resistant hES clones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of culture conditions to promote the undifferentiated hESC renewal and to efficiently generate hESC clones with desired genotypes for basic and translated research.
the development of a feeder-free system that can be used for the long-term maintenance of undifferentiated and genetically modified human embryonic stem cells.
the use of Wnt signaling and feeder cells in the propagation of human embryonic stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wnt3A and Wnt1 can promote hES cell growth and renewal, and the Wnt3A-overexpressing HAFi feeder (W3R feeder) can be used to select rare genetically modified hES cell clones.
Wnt3 and Wnt1 can be used in the culture of undifferentiated human embryonic stem cells, but Wnt5a is not.
Wnt3A, Wnt1 and bFGF can promote the growth of undifferentiate hES cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a system for the efficient propagation of hES cells in feeder-free culture conditions by modulating the Wnt signal.
Wnt signaling plays an important role in hES cell proliferation and differentiation, and can be manipulated to promote undifferentiated hESC growth.
Wnt3 and Wnt1 are potent mitogens for undifferentiated hESC and that Wnt3 can also promote the undifferentiated proliferation of hESC when feeder cells are also present.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Wnt ligands can be used to promote the growth of undifferentiate hES cell lines and to generate genetically modified hES cell clones.
Wnt3 and Wnt1 are important for hES cell proliferation and that Wnt3 is a good candidate for promoting the undifferentiated expansion of hES cells.
the Wnt signaling can be manipulated to promote hES cell growth and proliferation.
